lines.say: Arab citizens are twenty one percent of Israel. What share of its doctors?
Here's an apartheid test almost nobody runs. One twenty twenty five study, in the Israel Journal of Health Policy Research.
Start in twenty ten. Arab citizens are eight percent of doctors.
Seventeen percent of nurses. Nineteen percent of dentists.
Now watch twenty twenty three. Thirteen years later.
Doctors: twenty five percent. More than triple in thirteen years.
Nurses and dentists: twenty seven percent.
Pharmacists: forty nine percent. Almost half. Pick up medicine in Israel, and it's close to a coin flip that an Arab pharmacist hands it to you.
And of all new doctors licensed since twenty ten, thirty eight percent are Arab. That's the next generation of Israeli medicine.
The same study says real gaps and challenges remain. Equality is not finished.
So the next time someone says apartheid, ask them this:

data.unit: Arab citizens' share of each job (population 21%)

sources.label: Rosen and Miaari, Israel Journal of Health Policy Research

end.balance: Real gaps *remain.* This still isn't apartheid.

caption_en:
Arab citizens are 21% of Israel. Their share of its health workforce: 🩺

Doctors 8% (2010) to 25% (2023). Nurses 27%. Dentists 27%. Pharmacists 28% to 49%, almost half. Of new physician licences 2010 to 2022: 38%.

Source: Rosen B, Miaari S. "Arab representation in Israeli healthcare professions: achievements, challenges and opportunities", Israel Journal of Health Policy Research 14:7 (2025). 2023 shares include Arab residents of east Jerusalem; employed professionals up to age 67.

The same study says real gaps and challenges remain. This still isn't what apartheid looks like.

Send this to someone who says it is.
caption_he:
הערבים הם 21% מאזרחי ישראל. החלק שלהם במערכת הבריאות:
רופאים: מ-8% (2010) ל-25% (2023). אחיות ואחים 27%. רופאי שיניים 27%. רוקחים: מ-28% ל-49%, כמעט חצי. מהרישיונות החדשים לרופאים בין 2010 ל-2022: 38%.
אותו מחקר אומר שעדיין יש פערים ואתגרים אמיתיים. זה עדיין לא אפרטהייד.

Sources: Rosen B, Miaari S., Israel Journal of Health Policy Research 14:7 (2025), via PMC; JNS report (Feb 2025).
